summary: Koshu Itabashi (1927–2020) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Sendai Daiichi High School, the Imperial Japanese Naval Academy, and Tohoku University (~1949–1953), where he studied under Teruji Ishizu (~1948–1953).

Kosuke Nakazawa (born 1943) is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Guohui Shi. He held positions at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2001) and Rissho University, serving as professor (attested 2001) and professor emeritus (attested 2026).

Kotatsu Fujita (1928–2023) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Harvard, working under supervisors Shoson Miyamoto and Hajime Nakamura. He served at Osaka University (~1961–1968) and Hokkaido University (~1968–1992).

Kotetsu Yoshida (born 1941) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He has served as a professor emeritus at Taisho University (attested 2014) and as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).
Koun Kajiyoshi (1904–1984) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and held a post at Taisho University.

Koun Yamada (1907–1989) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the First Higher School and under several traditional teachers, including Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, whom he succeeded (1961–1989). Yamada also founded Kamakura Haku-un-kai in 1953.
Koyo Sakaino (1871–1933) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He founded Bukkyo Seito Doshikai and held posts at Toyo University (~1900–1923) and Komazawa University.
Koyo Shimizu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. Shimizu held a post as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1995).

Koyu Tamura (1931–2022) was a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who earned degrees at the University of Tokyo. He held positions at Nishogakusha University, the Department of Cultural Affairs, and Toyo University, serving there as associate professor (1972) and professor emeritus (1977–2000).

Kozen Shaku (1849–1924) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Senmyō. He served as abbot at Gyokuri-ji (1870–1881) and Sange-ji (1882), taught at Nagano Prefectural Northern Chugakurin (1881), and founded Shakuson Shofukai (1893).

Kozui Otani (1876–1948) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Gakushuin and Kyoritsu Gakusha under Eun Maeda, he served as the 22nd Abbot of Nishi Hongan-ji (1903–1914) and founded Kojukai (1919).
Kripa Shankar Shukla (1918–2007) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who held a post at the University of Lucknow until 1959, with his affiliation there also attested in 1976.

Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya (1840–1932) was an Indologist. He studied at Sanskrit College and University and Presidency University, later holding posts at Presidency University (1862–1872) and Surendranath College (1891–1903).

Krishna Kanta Handiqui (1898–1982) was an Indologist. He studied at Cotton University, Sanskrit College, Calcutta, Oxford, Paris, and Berlin. He served as Principal of Jorhat College (1930–1948) and Vice-Chancellor of Gauhati University (1948–1957), and founded Hemalata Handiqui Memorial Institute.

Krishna Mohan Banerjee (1813–1885) was an Indology, linguistics, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Hare School, Presidency University, and Bishop's College, Kolkata, learning from Alexander Duff. He held posts at Hare School (~1828–1831) and Bishop's College (1852).

Krishna Venkateswara Sarma (1919–2005) was an Indologist and historian educated at University College Thiruvananthapuram and the University of Kerala under V. A. Ramaswami Sastri. He held posts at Panjab University, the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute, and Adyar Library.

Krishnacharya Tammannacharya Pandurangi (1918–2017) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Bangalore University, Honorary Director of the Dvaita Vedanta Studies and Research Foundation, and Upakulapati at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha (attested 1997).

Krishnanath Chatterjee is an Indologist who studied under Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amarasvar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

Krishnaswamy Nachimuthu is an Indology and linguistics scholar. In 2021, he was attested holding a post at École française d'Extrême-Orient and serving as an editorial board member for Studies on the History of Śaivism.

Kristin Johnston Largen is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. She has held posts at Wartburg Theological Seminary, United Lutheran Seminary as Professor of Systematic Theology (attested 2018), and Gettysburg College (attested 2018).
